chunks: Had there been a Qur'an which could have made the mountains move, or the earth to cleave asunder, or the dead to speak, yet all authority belongs to God. Have the believers not learnt that if God had so willed He could have guided all mankind? As for unbelievers, they will be visited by misfortune endlessly for what they have done; or it would sit in their homes till the promised threat of God comes to pass. Surely God does not go back on His promise.

key_terms.يُخْلِفُ: to break or fail to fulfill

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean when it says it could move mountains or split the earth?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse addresses the Qur'anic skeptics' demand for miraculous signs, clarifying that the Quran itself is the ultimate miracle, though God reserves the power to manifest physical wonders like moving mountains or resurrecting the dead. It highlights the theological principle of divine will (Mashi'ah) versus human free will, noting that while God could compel belief, He chose to allow disbelievers to face consequences through 'Qari'ah' (calamities or strikes) as a gradual process until the final promise is fulfilled.
